meta.method: One row per jurisdiction whose official sources were read for a scope (fees, land_use, funds). "none_found" means the named sources were read and hold no such measure; "unreadable" means the official source could not be read (blocked, a scan with no text, or a dead link). A scope with a verified record is shown as having records whatever this file says; tests/test_local_incentives.py fails if a row says none_found for a scope that has a record. Jurisdictions not listed here and with no record are "not yet checked".

jurisdictions.note: Aurora's developer page offers only Community Investment Financing (CIF) gap financing from federal/PAB sources (2026 round 1: Private Activity Bonds, HOME, CDBG) — not a local dedicated fund, so not recorded. The 2020 Housing Strategy lists 'Waive or reduce development fees up to an annual amount' and a housing fund as recommendations only; no adopted program found on fee pages. City code (aurora.municipal.codes, incl. UDO ch. 146) returns 403 to scripted and WebFetch requests, so land-use incentives could not be verified.

sources_checked: https://library.municode.com/co/thornton/codes/code_of_ordinances (Municode API search: affordable, inclusionary, deed-restricted, income-restricted, housing fund)
jurisdictions.note: Thornton's housing page lists only HOME, CDBG and Private Activity Bonds as developer funding, plus letters of support; development and 2026 water/sewer connection fee schedules contain no affordable-housing reduction; code has no affordable-housing incentive. Page says the city has no down-payment program yet and plans to request ~$750,000 of Prop 123 DPA funds (state money, not recorded). A 2019 Denverite report of waived tap fees / rebated permits for Crossing Pointe North could not be read (403) and was not recorded.

sources_checked: https://library.municode.com/co/centennial/codes/municipal_code (Municode API search incl. Land Development Code ch. 12: affordable, attainable, inclusionary, deed-restricted, income restricted, fast track, Proposition 123)
jurisdictions.note: Municipal code (Supp. 26 Update 3, through Ord. 2026-O-07) has no affordable-housing fee relief or land-use incentive; only mention is the STR chapter purpose statement. centennialco.gov is blocked (Akamai 403), so any non-codified housing program or fund could not be read. A 2023 council housing-study update (search snippet only) listed expedited review and land banking as options.

sources_checked: https://library.municode.com/co/parker/codes/municipal_code (Municode API search: affordable, attainable, inclusionary, deed-restricted, income restricted, fast track, Proposition 123)
jurisdictions.note: Parker's code (Supp. 26.1) has no affordable-housing fee, zoning or fund provision. Per search results the Town has no housing authority of its own, is a member of the Douglas County Housing Partnership, joined DCHP's regional Prop 123 commitment (Oct 2023) and assigned PAB allocation to DCHP — none of these is a local incentive and the pages were not fetched, so nothing recorded.

Northglenn's code is not on library.municode.com but on the city-hosted municode.northglenn.org (northglenn.municipal.codes and amlegal returned 403). Fee/expedited-review/setback incentives are limited to the MX Mixed-Use Overlay; parking reduction is citywide. No housing fund, dedicated tax or linkage fee in code.

Code has a 'Housing Rehabilitation Fund' (4-3-6, 'housing rehabilitation activities') — not affordable-housing-specific, not recorded as a fund. englewoodco.gov blocked (403), so the 'Affordable Housing Fast Track' page and the impact-fee schedule could not be read; no expedited-review record created.
